limits: These are finite admission limits for requested buffers, not hard allocator/processRSS/GPU/global budgets.

ZIP compressed source is checked before construction. Entry count is checked afterward and does not bound constructor central-directory metadata allocation; ZIP9 may retry earlier EOCD candidates, so the Office single-footer preflight is not a proven general fix.

Expanded totals charge every actually materialized manifest/selectedJSON/image read including repeated paths; unused archive entries are not decompressed. Base64 strings can take about4/3 image bytes, and model/metadata allocations are additional.

Image working accounting includes native decoder output, RGBA conversion, target, actual cross-aspect RGBA32F intermediate and conservatively rounded sampling-weight capacities. Decoder-private allocations/image max_alloc enforcement remain best effort; allocator overhead is additional.

External resolver callbacks allocate before returning; per-return and aggregate guards reject their returned bytes before retaining/copying, but do not bound callback-owned allocation. Inline URLs live in the already-parsed model.
Decoded totals belong to one prepared animation, worker clones have independent budgets. Existing Kael cache uses only finite default policy; custom Kael policy was not added.
Upstream unused malformed image assets remain lazy. Public additive limits allow explicit raised/tighter policies, subject to checked arithmetic and isize buffer representability.
